title: The Metal That Remembers
hook: Right now, warm blood in your chest is forcing metal to remember its shape.
script: Right now, warm blood inside a patient's chest is forcing metal to remember its shape. What if you could crumple a wire and watch it heal itself? A shape memory alloy called nitinol does that under gentle heat. Its atoms shift into mirror images without breaking bonds, so it returns to shape. As this metal springs back, it exerts enough force to lift an anvil. Surgeons crush tiny nitinol stents in ice water so body heat springs them open inside blocked arteries. Heat does not weaken this alloy, it wakes it up.

captions: Does metal memory feel more like advanced engineering or biology?
Nitinol does not bend like normal steel—its atomic lattice simply tilts and snaps back.
Millions of people walk around with warm blood powering self-expanding nitinol stents.
